images.title: Four parts after one and a tenth
images.purpose: Show a wire ending 4 small parts after the 1 1/10 mark and the three equal ways to write its length.
images.composition: A number line across the upper middle with the wire above it; the three equal forms sit below, centred.
exact_structure: A horizontal line with a grey (#6B7280) double slash break between 0 and 1. Big marks labelled 0, 1, 1 1/10 and 1 2/10 in that order, with 1 to 1 1/10 and 1 1/10 to 1 2/10 as equal gaps.
Between 1 1/10 and 1 2/10 there are 9 small ticks, making 10 equal parts.
A teal (#0072B2) thick bar (the wire) starts at 0 and ends on the 4th small tick after 1 1/10. The 4 parts after 1 1/10 are shaded reddish purple (#CC79A7).
Below the line, centred, one row: 1 1/10 4/100 = 1 14/100 = 114/100.
rejection: the wire ends on a tick other than the 4th after 1 1/10
there are not 9 small ticks in the gap
the three written forms are not equal
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: One length can be written as units, tenths and hundredths, as units and hundredths, or all in hundredths.
images.description: A wire reaching four small parts past 1 1/10 on a scale, with its three equal fraction forms below.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Read the big marks first, then count the 4 small parts.

image_decisions.why: The picture ties the four small parts to the hundredths in each written form.
